project.name: Brunton (Creich)
project.boundarySource: Resolved named-place location with a conservative strict settlement study buffer
project.researchNotes: Brunton is rewarding to notice on foot, but it is not treated as a serviced tourist town. Strict-boundary score verified sequentially on 2026-09-02. Creich Castle and old church are retained under Creich rather than duplicated here. Private cottages and gardens are not visitor attractions. No shop, café, public toilet, picnic site or dedicated visitor car park was verified.

touristAppeal.label: Minor Interest
touristAppeal.summary: Brunton is a coherent conservation hamlet with unusually dense listed fabric and the official Fife Coastal Path, but no public visitor-service cluster. Its village character and route appear under See and Trails while the settlement remains below 60.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: The audited outdoor routes can suit responsible dog visits, with close control around livestock, roads, wildlife and historic fabric.

visitorHighlights.reason: A compact conservation hamlet of traditional cottages, former weaving structures and historic street form, best appreciated respectfully from public roads.
visitorHighlights.openingTimes: Public roads only; homes and gardens are private.

features.name: Manse, Creich
features.fullDescription: 1816. 2-storey basement and attic, 3-window front coursed whin rubble with ashlar dressings, R-doric column door piece with fanlight, railed steps to door. Gables harled and whitewashed. Original glazing. Slated roof, later canted dormers.
